title: Two loops for P(n)+P(n+2)
why: Collatz-type; f(n)<=2n+2 with twin-prime-like escape chains (n, n+2 both prime) impossible to rule out with current tools.

title: Three consecutive largest factors
why: Collatz-type largest-prime-factor map; no contraction argument controls rare orbits where P(n),P(n+2) both near n.

title: Three pairs
why: Collatz-type; growth steps need n, 2n+1 both prime (Sophie Germain pairs), uncontrollable.

title: Every binary block in Gerver's constant
why: Disjunctivity unknown even for sqrt2; Gerver area not even known irrational. Near-variant of existing 'Gerver constant is normal'.

title: An irrational sum over largest factors
why: Irrationality of arithmetic series like this has no known method; same flavour as existing 'Irrational prime weights'.

title: Smooth p²+1
why: Heuristically true; known smooth-value results for n²+1 (Dartyge, Harman) fall short of exponent 1/2 at prime arguments.

title: Large prime factors of 2^n + 3^n
why: Stewart gives only P(a^n-b^n)>n·exp(c log n/loglog n); exponent 2 far beyond current methods.

title: Sidon sets of seven-free numbers
why: Trivial bound sqrt(N); digit-wise constructions give only ~3^k vs sqrt(10^k), so the true order is a real question.

title: Prime Nim with Pythagorean primes
why: Variant of existing 'Infinite Prime Nim losses... show they are rare'; multiples of 4 avoid the moves, so no Sárközy shortcut.

title: The Hamiltonicity game on square sums
why: Min degree ~0.41sqrt(N), but Maker-Breaker results need pseudorandomness/expansion of S_N, itself open.

title: Prime Nim is not automatic
why: Same as existing 'Prime Nim is not automatic'.

title: Square-sum graph spectral gap
why: Same as existing 'Square-sum spectral gap' / 'Square-sum expansion' / 'Random walks on square sums'.

title: Infinite cube-sum paths
why: No obvious colouring counterexample (residue obstructions fail), and the increasing-path requirement blocks König-type arguments.

title: Erdős–Gyárfás in square sums
why: S_inf has infinite degrees, so the infinite 3-regular tree embeds greedily as a subgraph: min degree 3, no cycles at all.

title: Twin-prime-free sums
why: Evens give 1/2; if twin primes were finite the limit is 1, so determining the limit (1/2) implies infinitely many twin primes.

title: Stopping times of the doubling map
why: Close variant of existing 'Affine prime maps, quantitative' (3p+4); needs iterated P(2p+1) distribution, beyond EH-level. 8-cycle verified.

title: Lattice packing of the sofa
why: Gerver's parameters solve transcendental equations, not algebraic; 'closed form over Q(algebraic parameters)' has a false premise. Non-convex body.

title: Spectre Laplacian
why: Essentially existing 'Spectre drum eigenvalue is transcendental' (polygon instead of curved spectre); hopeless transcendence question.

title: Blow-up rate for the forced NS singularity
why: 'The' singularity is construction-dependent; forced constructions are typically self-similar by design, making the rate trivial; 'unique profile' undefined.

title: Periodic billiards in the hat
why: Same as existing 'Hat billiard counting'. Hat is rational polygon, so Masur's quadratic bounds known; exact asymptotic open.

title: Moser's worm in the sphere
why: Planar Moser worm not even pinned within 1%; spherical version at least as hard.

title: Cheeger constant of the sofa
why: Transcendence of a variational constant of a non-convex body; Gerver's area itself not known irrational.

title: Dimers on the hat tiling
why: Same as existing 'Hat dimers' (count coverings exactly per tile).

title: Random Prime Nim
why: Limit does not exist: parity/local primes matter (if 2 not in R, evens are mostly P). Simulation: odd n ~0.96, even n ~0.55-0.82.

title: Random sequential prime-sum packing
why: Bipartite odd/even race; answer likely 1/2 via one parity winning; needs prime equidistribution but seems standard.

title: Glauber dynamics on hat tiling Potts
why: Hat vertex graph is not self-dual, so 'self-dual point' is undefined; overlaps existing 'Potts transition on hats'.

title: Sharp threshold for prime-sum Hamiltonicity
why: Degree ~2n/log n gives p ~ log²n/n; requires sieve-based pseudorandomness of codegrees, plausible but technical.

title: Prime factor plus digit sum
why: Non-primes contract; must rule out infinite prime chains p->p+s(p), Cunningham-chain-like and out of reach.

title: The field of Gerver's sofa
why: Premise false (parameters not known algebraic); answer amounts to existing 'Gerver constant is transcendental'/'algebraic independence of angles'.

title: Formal verification depth of RH
why: Instance of Friedman's grand conjecture; likely yes via WKL0 conservativity over IΣ1, but demands reworking the whole proof.

title: Square subtraction with prime piles
why: Subtract-a-square P-positions are sparse and structureless; primes in them is like existing 'Square losses in Prime Nim', hopeless.

title: Seven-free factorial-like products
why: Akin to Erdős's 2^n digit problems; fixed blocks of last nonzero digits (automatic) likely avoid 7 infinitely often.

title: Largest prime factor of 2^n + n
why: Known lower bounds via linear forms in logs are ~log n scale; superlinear in n far beyond.

title: Book thickness of the square-sum graph
why: S_N has ~cN^{3/2} edges but k pages hold <=k(2N-3) edges, so bt >= c·sqrt(N): unbounded.
